analysis: The fluidity of the plasma membrane is influenced by the types of fatty acids present in the phospholipids that make up the membrane. Unsaturated fatty acids, such as arachidonic acid, have one or more double bonds in their hydrocarbon chains, which introduce kinks that prevent the fatty acids from packing tightly together. This results in increased membrane fluidity. Arachidonic acid, being an unsaturated fatty acid, fits this description and thus increases the fluidity of the plasma membrane by being incorporated into phospholipids and enhancing unsaturation. Cholesterol also plays a role in modulating membrane fluidity, but its effect is concentration-dependent, making it a less straightforward choice. Both palmitic and stearic acids are saturated fats and would decrease membrane fluidity by allowing the fatty acid chains to pack more closely. Based on the consensus in physiological understanding of membrane dynamics, arachidonic acid is the most likely correct answer.
